evidence: Python/config_manager.py line 349: 'config_manager = ConfigManager()' — module-level singleton created at import time; ConfigManager.__init__ sets self.config_file = './config/active_inference_config.json' with a relative path that depends on the CWD at import time, not at call time

Python/serializer.py line 426: 'serializer = Serializer()' — module-level singleton; Serializer.__init__ calls 'os.makedirs(self.checkpoint_path, exist_ok=True)' at import time — a file I/O side effect on module load

Python/teacher_wrapper.py lines 6-7: 'lib_path = os.path.join(...)' and 'teacher_lib = ctypes.CDLL(lib_path)' — module-level ctypes.CDLL load at import time; if the .so file does not exist, the entire module fails to import with an OSError; no lazy loading or conditional import

reporting_system.py lines 27-28: 'plt.style.use(...); sns.set_palette(...)' — matplotlib/seaborn global state mutated at module import time; any code that imports this module inherits these style settings whether or not it wants them

Shell/config.sh lines 66-69: 'if ! validate_config; then exit 1' — validation runs at source time (import time equivalent); the exit 1 will terminate the sourcing process, which is correct behavior but means config.sh cannot be sourced speculatively

Shell/run.sh lines 22-38: if config.sh does not exist, run.sh creates a new config.sh with hardcoded content — this mutates the filesystem as a side effect of running the entry point script, coupling initialization to execution

benchmark_suite.py __init__: 'self.results_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True); self.plots_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)' — directory creation at constructor time; constructing an AdvancedBenchmarkSuite always creates output directories even when they are not needed
master_controller.py __init__: 'self.output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)' — same pattern: directory creation at object construction time
reporting_system.py main(): 'Path("visualizations").mkdir(exist_ok=True)' at top of main() — CWD-relative directory creation; coupled to the CWD at script invocation time with no override mechanism

master_controller.py _run_language() line 195: 'os.chdir(lang_dir)' — changes the process CWD as a side effect of running a language; if an exception occurs before 'os.chdir(self.root_dir)' on line 197, the CWD is permanently changed for all subsequent operations in the process

Shell/Active_Shellference.sh: global variables 'declare -A simulation', 'declare -i time_steps', 'declare -i precision' are initialized by initialize_simulation() which must be called before run_simulation(); no enforcement of this call order

strengths: Shell/Active_Shellference.sh loads config.sh with a script-relative path (SCRIPT_DIR), avoiding CWD-sensitive path resolution for config loading
benchmark_suite.py uses pathlib.Path throughout for path construction rather than string concatenation, reducing path-resolution bugs
master_controller.py stores root_dir as Path(__file__).parent — import-relative anchoring is correct and CWD-independent for path base
initialization_coupling.issue_character: Module-level singletons created at import time perform filesystem side effects (directory creation, .so loading, file I/O), and the process CWD is mutated mid-execution as a substitute for passing a working directory to subprocesses.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: Two module-level singletons (config_manager, serializer) execute filesystem side effects at import time, one ctypes load will crash the import on any machine without the .so present, matplotlib/seaborn global state is set at import time, and os.chdir() mid-execution creates a fragile CWD dependency. These are systemic rather than isolated: a test that imports any of these modules in isolation risks creating directories, mutating global plot state, or failing to import entirely. The score is in the lower third — initialization coupling is not accidental in one place but structural across the Python layer.

issues.summary: Python/serializer.py creates checkpoint directory at module import time via module-level Serializer() singleton
evidence: Line 426: 'serializer = Serializer()' at module scope
Serializer.__init__ line 31: 'os.makedirs(self.checkpoint_path, exist_ok=True)' — filesystem write at import time
Any module that imports serializer.py immediately creates './checkpoints/' in the current directory
issues.suggestion: Remove the module-level 'serializer = Serializer()' singleton; let callers construct Serializer instances explicitly. Defer directory creation to the first actual save operation.

issues.summary: Python/config_manager.py module-level ConfigManager singleton uses CWD-relative path set at import time
evidence: Line 349: 'config_manager = ConfigManager()' at module scope
ConfigManager.__init__ line 123: 'self.config_file = "./config/active_inference_config.json"' — relative to CWD at import time
If the module is imported from a different directory, the config file path silently points to the wrong location
issues.suggestion: Remove the module-level singleton; document that callers should construct ConfigManager with an explicit base_dir argument anchored to __file__ or a passed root path

issues.summary: Python/teacher_wrapper.py loads a .so via ctypes.CDLL at module scope, crashing import if the file is absent
evidence: Line 7: 'teacher_lib = ctypes.CDLL(lib_path)' at module scope
lib_path points to '../C/teacher_model.so' — a compiled artifact that may not exist
ImportError/OSError at import time with no fallback; any code that imports teacher_wrapper will fail on machines without the compiled C library
issues.suggestion: Wrap the ctypes.CDLL in a try/except at module level with a clear error message, or use lazy loading: load the .so inside TeacherModel.__init__ only when actually instantiated

issues.summary: reporting_system.py mutates matplotlib and seaborn global style at module import time
evidence: Lines 27-28: 'plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid"); sns.set_palette("husl")' at module scope
Any process that imports reporting_system.py inherits these plot styles for all subsequent matplotlib/seaborn calls, regardless of intent
issues.suggestion: Move plt.style.use() and sns.set_palette() inside the specific methods that create plots, or inside a setup_plotting_style() function that callers opt into explicitly

issues.summary: master_controller._run_language() uses os.chdir() to set CWD and cannot restore it if an exception occurs
evidence: Lines 195-197: 'os.chdir(lang_dir); subprocess.run(["./run.sh"]); os.chdir(self.root_dir)'
If subprocess.run raises (e.g., FileNotFoundError), os.chdir(self.root_dir) is never called
All subsequent _run_language() calls operate from the wrong directory
issues.suggestion: Replace os.chdir + subprocess.run with subprocess.run(..., cwd=lang_dir) to pass the working directory without mutating the process CWD

issues.summary: Shell/run.sh creates a new config.sh as a side effect of running, potentially overwriting user configuration
evidence: Lines 22-38: 'if [ ! -f config.sh ]; then cat > config.sh << CONFIG_EOF ... CONFIG_EOF fi'
The embedded config has different default values than the actual config.sh (e.g., CONFIG_TIME_STEPS=50 vs 15)
A developer who deletes config.sh to reset state gets a different configuration than the canonical one
issues.suggestion: Remove config.sh generation from run.sh; ensure config.sh is tracked in version control or explicitly documented as required before running

root_causes: Module-level singletons were created as convenience shortcuts without considering import-time side effects — a pattern common in AI/ML Python scripts where global objects (models, configs) feel natural at module scope
os.chdir() used as a CWD management strategy rather than subprocess cwd= parameter — suggests the subprocess API was not fully understood or the scripts predate the cwd= convention
possible_false_positives: Shell/config.sh exit on validation failure — this is an intentional error boundary at the configuration entry point, not a coupling problem
